html:
Zhou Daguan was a Chinese envoy who lived at Angkor in 1296 and 1297 with an embassy from the Yuan court. His book, The Customs of Cambodia, is the only first-hand account of life in the Khmer capital.

He described the golden towers of Angkor Thom, royal processions, markets run by women, slaves from the hill peoples, Chinese traders, festivals and bathing in the rivers. He noted three religions: Brahmins, Buddhist monks and Shaivite ascetics.

His text was translated into French in the 19th century and guided the first modern study of Angkor. He saw the empire after Jayavarman VII, in a period when Theravada Buddhism was spreading.
sum: Zhou Daguan was a Chinese envoy who lived at Angkor in 1296 and 1297 with an embassy from the Yuan court. His book, The Customs of Cambodia, is the only first-hand account of life in the Khmer capital.
